chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'd Abadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Ayyub, from Abd al-Salam al-Iskafi, from Umayr ibn Ma'mun (whose daughter was married to al-Hasan), from al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them) who said:

The gift of the fasting man is that he oils his beard and perfumes his garment, and the gift of the fasting woman is that she combs her hair and perfumes her garment. And Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them) would, when he fasted, apply perfume and say: 'Perfume is the gift of the fasting person.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended grooming practices for a fasting person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* elevates personal grooming from mere hygiene to a spiritual 'gift' (tahfah) of the fasting state, reflecting the Shia emphasis on beauty and cleanliness as acts of worship. It specifically highlights the practice of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who would perfume himself while fasting, thereby linking physical presentation with spiritual devotion. This tradition underscores the holistic nature of fasting in Shia jurisprudence, where external appearance serves as an expression of internal reverence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-86 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufy, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ayoob, on the authority of Abdul-Salam al-Iskafi, on the authority of Umayr ibn Ma’mun whose son was with Al-Hassan (MGB) , on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali (MGB), “

The gift from a man who fasts is that he puts perfume on his hair and irons his clothes, and the gift from a woman who fasts is to comb her hair and iron her clothes. When Abu Abdullah al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB) fasted, he (MGB) put on perfume and said, ‘Good scent is the gift from one who fasts.’”
